comments.title: Electric Easement Surface Material Not Specified on Grading Plan
comments.comment: The grading plan does not specify any surface material within electric easement areas, so compliance with the all-weather paved-surface requirement cannot be verified.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.3.16 requires all-weather drivable surfaces—HMAC or PCC pavement capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight (32,530 lbs max rear axle)—within electric easements for AE maintenance truck access. LDC § 25-12-173 Section 202.1 defines 'All Weather Driving Surface' as HMAC or PCC only; grass, gravel, and unpaved surfaces do not qualify. Sheet 11 shows easement boundaries with contour lines and labels but includes no surface material callouts, hatching, or legend entries for any electric easement area. Sheet 21 suggests eastern and southeastern transformer locations may be in landscaped or tree-canopy zones, raising further concern that those easement surfaces are unpaved.
comments.sheets: Grading plan (Sheet 11); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All electric easement areas on site, including the 5' electric easements along the eastern and southeastern property boundaries, the 5' Elec. & Tele. Easement, and all 5' P.U.E. areas
comments.resolution: Add notes, material callouts, hatching, and legend entries to the grading plan (Sheet 11) specifying that all surfaces within electric easement areas shall be HMAC or PCC pavement capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight (32,530 lbs max rear axle weight). Where easement areas are currently shown as or implied to be grass, gravel, or unpaved, revise the design to provide compliant paved surfaces or provide written AE approval for an alternative surface treatment.

perRunFindings.comment: Drivable surfaces within electric easements are not specified on the grading plan. The plan shows easement boundaries but provides no notes indicating whether surfaces will be paved (HMAC or PCC), grass, gravel, or other materials. Please add notes to the grading plan (Sheet 11) specifying that all-weather surfaces (hot mix asphalt concrete or Portland cement concrete) capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight will be provided within all electric easement areas to accommodate maintenance vehicles.
applicableAreas: All electric easement areas on site

perRunFindings.comment: Drivable surfaces within electric easements are not labeled or specified. Provide explicit surface material specifications (HMAC or PCC pavement) for all electric easement areas on the grading plan and construction details, demonstrating that surfaces are capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight and 32,530 lbs rear axle weight. If any electric easement areas are not paved all-weather surfaces, revise grading/landscaping to provide such surfaces or provide written approval from Austin Energy for alternative surface treatment.
applicableAreas: All electric easement areas shown on grading plan

perRunFindings.comment: Drivable surfaces within electric easements not suitable for maintenance vehicles and large bucket trucks; surfaces are unpaved, grass, gravel, or otherwise inadequate for heavy equipment. No surface material specification is provided for the 5-foot electric easements. Specify that all electric easement areas shall be graded and paved with HMAC or PCC concrete capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight. Provide a grading and paving plan for all electric easement access routes, showing the surface specification and confirming that maintenance vehicle access is maintained along the full length of easements.
applicableAreas: Electric easement areas, particularly the 5-foot electric easements along eastern and southeastern property boundaries

comments.title: Transformer Pad Distance to Drivable Surface Undimensioned; Design Incomplete
comments.comment: No dimension callouts verify that any of the four transformer pads are within 6 feet of a drivable surface, and the electrical plan contains an explicit notation that the transformer pad detail is incomplete.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.3.16 and § 1.10.4 require equipment pads to be within 6 feet of a parking/traffic area for truck accessibility, or—if more than 6 feet away—served by a 20-foot all-weather access route. Neither the site plan nor the electrical plan provides dimension callouts from any transformer pad to the nearest drivable surface. A handwritten note on Sheet 21 adjacent to a transformer pad reads 'need to look up approp. detail,' indicating the design is incomplete. Eastern pads (near Buildings 4–7) appear sited within landscaped areas with tree canopies, raising concern that those locations are not paved and may exceed the 6-foot threshold. Run-2 (EL-14.1) observed that Transformer 2 appears within approximately 2 feet of a parking space but lacks any dedicated access easement or dimensioned route documentation.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: All four transformer pad locations: west of Buildings 1 and 2, between Buildings 4 and 5, between Buildings 6 and 7, and west of Building 8 (vault easement); eastern pads of particular concern
comments.resolution: Provide dimension callouts on the site plan (Sheet 9) or electrical plan (Sheet 21) from each transformer pad to the nearest parking/traffic area, confirming each is within 6 feet. Resolve the incomplete design note ('need to look up approp. detail') with a complete, referenced transformer pad detail. For any pad exceeding 6 feet from a drivable surface, show a dimensioned 20-foot all-weather access route or provide written AE approval for an alternative configuration.

perRunFindings.comment: 24/7 truck access to transformer locations is not shown or dimensioned. Four transformer pads are depicted on the electrical design plan and shown adjacent to internal driveways, but no dimensions confirm that pads are within 6 feet of a drivable surface per UCM § 1.10.4. Please dimension the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest drivable surface (parking area or driveway) and confirm that all transformers are located within 6 feet of a paved surface capable of supporting truck access.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations

perRunFindings.comment: 24/7 truck access to transformer pad locations is not clearly shown or dimensioned on plans. Provide dimension callouts from each of the four transformer pad locations to the nearest accessible parking or traffic area, demonstrating that all transformers are within 6 feet of all-weather drivable surface suitable for bucket truck access per UCM § 1.10.4. If any transformer is more than 6 feet from accessible parking/traffic area, relocate or provide written approval from Austin Energy demonstrating acceptable maintenance access methodology.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations shown on electrical design plan and site plan

perRunFindings.comment: 24/7 truck access to transformer locations not provided, shown on plans, or is obstructed by site improvements, fencing, or other features. Transformer pad locations are shown but access design is incomplete (noted as 'need to look up approp. detail'). No dimensioned access route from parking areas is provided, and distances from transformer pads to drivable surfaces are not verified. Provide detailed access plans for each transformer pad showing: (1) dimensioned distance from each pad to adjacent parking/traffic surfaces (must be within 6 feet), (2) surface specifications for access routes (HMAC or PCC pavement capable of supporting bucket truck weight), and (3) complete transformer pad detail that confirms truck accessibility for installation, operation, and maintenance.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations on west and east sides of the site

perRunFindings.comment: Distance from transformer pads to nearest drivable surface not dimensionally verified on plans. Provide dimensioned measurements from each transformer pad to the nearest drivable surface, confirming either that pads are within 6 feet of drivable surface, or alternatively that 20-foot all-weather access routes are provided where pads exceed 6 feet from drivable surfaces.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pad 2 is located directly adjacent to parking with less than 2 feet of clearance. Site plan does not show a dedicated 20-foot all-weather truck access route for this transformer. Provide either: (1) a documented dedicated truck access easement at least 20 feet long to the transformer pad, or (2) demonstrated coordination with Austin Energy confirming the parking lot access is acceptable for transformer truck operations.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad 2 (eastern location, between Bldg. 4 and 5)

comments.title: Transformer Pads Missing Required 20'×35' Setup Area, 35' Vertical Clearance, and Clear Zone
comments.comment: No 20-foot × 35-foot setup area or 35-foot vertical clearance is shown or dimensioned at any transformer pad location, and trees and tree wells immediately adjacent to the pads obstruct the required clear zones.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.3.16 requires a minimum 20 ft × 35 ft horizontal clear zone with 35 ft vertical clearance in front of each pad-mounted transformer for crane/bucket truck access. The following deficiencies exist across plans:
- No setup area boundaries, dimensions, or designations are shown on any plan sheet for any of the four transformer pads
- No vertical clearance analysis or annotation is provided; buildings near transformer locations are 33 ft–36 ft tall, making vertical clearance compliance uncertain
- Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows large circular tree canopy symbols overlapping or immediately adjacent to all three or four transformer pad locations
- Sheet 9 (Site Plan) identifies a labeled 'Tree Well' immediately adjacent (within 2–5 feet) to the westernmost transformer pad (near Bldg. 1/2)
- Landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show transformer pad locations or their staging zones, so landscaping conflicts cannot be verified; no notation excludes trees or shrubs from required clear zones
- No AE Design written approval of any deviation from standard clearance requirements is included in the plan set
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site plan (Sheet 9); Landscape plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: All transformer pad locations: west of Buildings 1 and 2 (directly adjacent to labeled Tree Well), between Buildings 4 and 5, between Buildings 6 and 7, and west of Building 8
comments.resolution: On Sheets 9 and 21, dimension and designate the required 20 ft × 35 ft horizontal clear zone in front of each transformer pad. Verify and annotate 35 ft vertical clearance above each pad; provide building sections or overhead clearance notes if buildings or canopies encroach within the clearance envelope. Remove or relocate the tree well and any trees or landscaping within all required clear zones, or provide written AE Design approval for any deviation with approval conditions noted on plans. Add transformer pad locations and their clear zone boundaries to the landscape plan (Sheet 31) with a note prohibiting all trees, shrubs, and hardscape within those zones.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Removal or relocation of proposed trees (including tree wells and parking lot trees shown on Sheet 31) may require coordination with the City Arborist if any trees qualify for protection; landscape plan revisions will also require coordination with the landscape reviewer.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Medium confidence for setup area and tree obstruction issues (2/3 runs); vertical clearance finding is low confidence (1/3 runs)—reviewer should verify whether buildings adjacent to transformer locations (33–36 ft heights) restrict the 35 ft vertical clearance requirement.

perRunFindings.comment: 20-foot × 35-foot set-up area with 35-foot vertical clearance not dimensionally verified on plans. Provide dimensioned site plan details showing the 20 ft × 35 ft set-up area in front of each transformer pad, with clearance to buildings, structures, and other obstructions, and confirm 35-foot vertical clearance above each pad is maintained.
applicableAreas: All four transformer pad locations

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pads lack required clear zone: 20-foot × 35-foot set-up area in front of transformer equipment not maintained. Trees and tree wells immediately adjacent to transformer pads obstruct required vertical clearance and set-up depth.
applicableAreas: All three transformer pad locations (west side near Buildings 1/8, and two on east side near Buildings 4 and 6)

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pad 1 is directly adjacent to a tree well, which obstructs access and creates a site feature blocking the required clear zone around the transformer. Remove the tree well or relocate the transformer to a site location that is free of landscaping, trees, tree wells, and other obstructions within a minimum 20 ft × 35 ft clear set-up area. Alternatively, provide documented coordination with Austin Energy Design and the arborist confirming the tree well can be modified or removed to provide unobstructed transformer access.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad 1 (western edge, adjacent to Bldg. 2)
Tree well and landscaping area near Transformer 1

perRunFindings.comment: Site features (trees, landscaping in tree wells) blocking access to transformer pads. Transformer pads not kept clear of all structures and landscaping for Austin Energy 24/7 access.
applicableAreas: All three transformer pad locations

perRunFindings.comment: Landscape plans do not demonstrate that landscaping avoids required staging areas adjacent to transformer locations. Please: (1) show all transformer pad locations and their 20' × 35' staging areas (with 35' vertical clearance) on the landscape plan; (2) add note stating no landscaping (trees, shrubs, hardscape) is permitted within these clear zones; (3) provide detail showing how existing landscaping plan respects transformer access requirements.
applicableAreas: Areas adjacent to transformer pad locations

perRunFindings.comment: No setup areas (minimum 20 feet × 35 feet horizontal) are shown in front of any of the four transformer pads. Design must designate and dimension the required crane/bucket truck access space for each piece of AE equipment per UCM § 1.3.16.
applicableAreas: Equipment setups in front of four transformer pads

perRunFindings.comment: No vertical clearance (minimum 35 feet) is shown or verified above any transformer pad. Building elevations are required to demonstrate adequate clearance for crane/bucket truck access, or alternative equipment locations must be provided.
applicableAreas: Vertical clearance space above equipment setups

perRunFindings.comment: Adequate set-up area and clearances at transformer equipment not documented, and AE Design approval of any deviations not shown. Provide either (1) dimensioned plans confirming 20 ft × 35 ft set-up area with 35-foot vertical clearance at all transformers, or (2) documented AE Design written approval of specific project deviations with approval conditions clearly noted on plans.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations

comments.title: Truck Access Paths to Transformer Pads Not Designated, Dimensioned, or Specified
comments.comment: No truck access paths to AE transformer equipment are labeled, dimensioned for minimum width or vertical clearance, specified for surface material, or documented for structural load capacity.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.3.16 requires truck access paths to AE facilities to satisfy all of the following, none of which are documented on the submitted plans:
- Minimum 12 ft horizontal width: no dimension callouts are provided along any route to any transformer pad
- Minimum 16 ft vertical clearance: no vertical clearance analysis is shown; grading plan (Sheet 11) omits transformer pad locations and elevations, making clearance verification impossible; building heights range from 33 ft to 36 ft in proximity to pad locations
- All-weather surface (HMAC or PCC): no surface material is specified for transformer pad access areas; pads appear within landscaped islands on Sheet 9, which may be unpaved
- Structural capacity supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight / 32,530 lbs max rear axle: no pavement design calculations or engineering certification are provided for any access surface
comments.sheets: Site plan (Sheet 9); Grading plan (Sheet 11); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All access paths to transformer pad locations throughout the site
comments.resolution: On the site plan (Sheet 9), label and dimension the truck access route to each transformer pad, confirming a minimum 12 ft horizontal width at the narrowest point. Annotate 16 ft vertical clearance along all access routes, providing building sections or overhead clearance notes where eaves, canopies, or other structures cross above. Specify HMAC or PCC pavement for all transformer pad access surfaces with callouts on Sheets 9 and 11. Provide pavement design calculations or a licensed engineer's certification confirming access surfaces support 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight (32,530 lbs max rear axle).
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs for each sub-item) — reviewer should verify whether standard driveway construction details already on file (e.g., Type III Driveway Detail 433S-2 referenced on Sheet 9) already document surface type and load capacity sufficient to address portions of this finding.

perRunFindings.comment: No truck access path (minimum 12 feet width, 16 feet vertical clearance) is designated or dimensioned on site plan or electrical plan. Design must identify the truck access route(s) to all AE equipment and dimension them to verify compliance with UCM § 1.3.16 standards, including surface load rating specifications.
applicableAreas: Access paths to transformer pads and electrical equipment throughout the site

perRunFindings.comment: Horizontal width of truck access paths to transformer pads not dimensionally verified. Provide dimensioned site plan showing minimum 12-foot width access route from drivable surface to each transformer pad, measured at the narrowest point of the access path.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad access routes

perRunFindings.comment: Vertical clearance of truck access paths to transformer pads not verified. Provide grading plan or building section details showing transformer pad locations with spot elevations, and verify that minimum 16-foot vertical clearance is maintained along all access routes to transformer pads, including clearances from building eaves, overhangs, and any other overhead structures.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad access routes

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pad access surfaces not specified as hot mix asphaltic concrete (HMAC) or Portland cement concrete (PCC) pavement. Provide detailed construction specifications and engineering calculations confirming that all transformer pad access surfaces meet all-weather pavement requirements and load capacity standards.
applicableAreas: All four transformer pad locations on electrical plan

perRunFindings.comment: Structural capacity of transformer pad access surfaces not documented. Provide pavement design calculations and structural engineering certification confirming that all transformer pad access surfaces can support 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight (32,530 lbs maximum rear axle weight) without damage.
applicableAreas: All four transformer pad locations on electrical plan

comments.title: No AE Vehicle Turnaround Provided at Dead-End Eastern Drive Aisle
comments.comment: The eastern drive aisle serving Buildings 3–6 and adjacent transformer pads terminates in a dead-end configuration with no turnaround area for Austin Energy maintenance trucks.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.3.16 requires that AE maintenance vehicles have the ability to turn around or exit the property. The eastern drive aisle terminates at a curb-and-gutter line with a retaining wall beyond, with no hammerhead, T-turn, cul-de-sac, or other labeled turning area shown for AE bucket trucks. Four transformer pads on the site require periodic service access, including from the eastern side of the property.
comments.applicableArea: Eastern drive aisle terminus serving Buildings 3–6
comments.resolution: Revise the site plan (Sheet 9) to provide a turnaround area—such as a hammerhead, T-turn, or cul-de-sac—at the eastern drive aisle terminus sufficient for AE bucket trucks. Label and dimension the turnaround area and confirm it meets UCM § 1.3.16 minimum requirements for AE vehicle maneuvering.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should confirm on Sheet 9 whether the eastern drive aisle truly dead-ends or connects to a circulation loop that would allow AE vehicles to exit without reversing.

perRunFindings.comment: AE vehicle turnaround or exit capability not provided. Revise site plan to provide a turnaround area (hammerhead, T-turn, or cul-de-sac) at the eastern drive aisle terminus with minimum dimensions per UCM § 1.3.16 (minimum 20 feet × 35 feet set-up area with 35 feet vertical clearance for AE vehicles). Show AE truck access routing and confirm turn-around capability.
applicableAreas: Eastern drive aisle terminus
Dead-end access for emergency and utility vehicles
